dossier.public_summary: The dip is on the target star, but its depth changes dramatically from sector to sector and from transit to transit, with some transits much deeper and some absent. A true planet on a 6.5-day orbit should repeat with the same depth, so the highly variable signal is best explained by noise, detrending or stellar variability rather than a planet.

reasons.why: Depth is not consistent at all; consistent planet dips should be stable.

Depth truly changes within the same pipeline, not a calibration offset between products. Sectors 32,43,44,70,71,1751 show essentially no or negative depth while sector 5 shows 652 ppm and sector 43 shows 2915 ppm.
Individual transits are highly inconsistent; a few extreme events drive the signal, classic for systematics or spurious dips rather than a repeating planet.

reasons.why: Difference imaging puts the dip on the target and rules out a neighbour blend, so the variation is on-target but is not a planet transit.
